solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thus may rap artiste show discipline?

parts.note: read the phrase in the grid as an instruction: a rearrangement of the ten letters before the last word, signalled by 'off', spells these two clue words

explanation.surface: A rapper, perhaps, shows how to keep people in line.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: take the first ten letters of the answer, scramble them ('off' as in gone off), and you get RAP ARTISTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a severe telling-off is an idiom for reprimanding, a way of disciplining them.

clue.text: For Wes to sew, maybe, is a progressive volte-face

parts.note: west, east and south are three compass points, and turning that trio round changes the first word into the last

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a man named Wes taking up needlework as a complete change of direction.
explanation.walkthrough: W, E and S are each a compass point; turn the three round and WES becomes SEW, which is what 'to sew' shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A driving manoeuvre that turns a car to face the other way in stages: forward, back, forward.

clue.text: Louse lay low beneath a piano

indicators.note: beneath in a down clue puts the lying-low piece below the other letters

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft
hid means stayed out of sight, lay low

explanation.surface: A louse hiding underneath a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenfly and blackfly are known as plant lice, small sap-sucking insects.

clue.text: This mad manager produces the answer

definitions.text: This mad manager produces the answer

indicators.note: produces the answer says the letters of the words before it are reworked to give what goes in the grid

explanation.surface: A crazy boss comes up with the solution.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes itself: the letters of MAD MANAGER, rearranged, give the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something whose letters have been rearranged into another word, which is what has happened to the clue's two words.

clue.text: Card lets dubious 21 enter international bar

indicators.note: enter says the jumbled letters go inside the card

parts.note: a ten is a playing card

indicators.note: dubious says the letters of the other answer are of doubtful arrangement and are reshuffled

parts.note: the answer to 21 across, a word for curtains or pills

explanation.surface: A card permitting doubtful pills into a cross-border bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty between nations prohibiting nuclear weapons testing is a prohibition, an international bar.

clue.text: Run-down old company with time becomes illegitimate

parts.note: run-down means unwell, ill
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British company

explanation.surface: A failing old firm that runs out of time ends up being outlawed.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI, Imperial Chemical Industries, was a major British chemical firm, broken up in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means not permitted by law or rule, which is a sense of illegitimate.

clue.text: Club raised, knock end off — clumsy me!

indicators.note: knock end off says the last letter is removed
raised in a down clue means the club is written upwards, the other way round

parts.note: a spoon is an old wooden-headed golf club

explanation.surface: Someone lifts a club, knocks the end off something, and blames their own clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoon is an old name for a lofted golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation one makes on dropping or knocking something over, admitting clumsiness.

clue.text: Lights on landing of apartment receiving major share of overhaul; try halogen for starters?

indicators.note: receiving says the apartment takes the shortened word inside it

parts.note: a flat is an apartment

indicators.note: major share of keeps the first four of six letters, dropping the tail

parts.note: to repair is to overhaul

indicators.note: for starters picks the opening letter of halogen

explanation.surface: Lighting for the landing of a flat being renovated, with halogen bulbs suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'try' gives no letter here: taking its first letter too would add an extra T, an apparent slip the blog also noted.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare path is the line of lights marking a runway so aircraft can land in poor visibility.

clue.text: Books with which no Rev is unfamiliar?

definitions.text: Books with which no Rev is unfamiliar?

parts.words: Books with which no Rev is unfamiliar?
parts.note: the books of the Bible, which every clergyman knows, in a particular English translation of 1881-85

explanation.surface: Volumes every vicar knows well.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1880s British revision of the King James Bible, a set of books a clergyman would know.

clue.text: For practice, include corny items among fabulous Lehar

indicators.note: include tells us one set of letters is to be taken in by another
among places the corny items within the other letters
fabulous, in the sense of fanciful or invented, says the composer's name is rearranged

parts.note: items of corn are ears, the heads of the cereal plant

explanation.surface: An instruction for a run-through of a Lehar operetta, padding it with some corny bits.
explanation.walkthrough: Ears of corn are the cereal heads, so the corny items are these; Lehar is the Hungarian operetta composer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is a practice session held before a performance.

clue.text: Smoother surface

definitions.meaning: a carpenter's tool that smooths wood
a flat level surface in geometry

explanation.surface: Two words that seem to describe a glossier finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane is both the woodworking tool used to smooth timber and a flat level surface in geometry.

clue.text: Ancestor of Daniel Deronda

indicators.note: of here means taken from within: the letters come from inside the novel's title

explanation.surface: Looks like a question about the family tree of George Eliot's hero Daniel Deronda.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the gap between the two words of the title.
explanation.definitionFit: An elder is a forebear or senior member of a family line, so it can stand for an ancestor.

clue.text: King's carriage reversing! Help!

indicators.note: reversing says the king's letter followed by the carriage are read the other way round

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a cab is a horse-drawn or hired carriage

explanation.surface: A cry for help as the king's coach rolls backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To back someone is to support or help them.

clue.text: Dash into heart of opposition's place

indicators.note: into says the dash goes inside the central letters
heart of picks the central pair of letters of the word opposition

parts.note: an em is a printer's dash, the width of a letter M

explanation.surface: Someone rushing into the opposition's home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: An em dash is a long printer's dash; it goes into SI, the two central letters of 'opposition'.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home, so a place where someone lives.

clue.text: And in Germany, over the outskirts of Wiesbaden, Roger manoeuvred and stunted

indicators.note: over in a down clue puts the earlier letters on top of what follows

parts.note: the German for and is und

indicators.note: manoeuvred says the name is moved around into a new order
outskirts of takes the outside letters of the city name

explanation.surface: Someone named Roger driving around the edge of Wiesbaden in Germany, and coming to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: UND, ERGRO (Roger rearranged) and WN (the ends of Wiesbaden).
explanation.definitionFit: Undergrown describes something that has not grown to full size, so it is stunted.

clue.text: He has a row as Norma breaks down

indicators.note: breaks down says the letters of the words collapse and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A man quarrels as his partner Norma breaks down in tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; here it is rowing a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower pulls an oar, so he is a man who has a row in the boating sense.

clue.text: With noise of disapproval, artists lead tiddly medium away …

parts.note: RAs are Royal Academicians, artists
Pb is the chemical symbol for lead

indicators.note: away says the medium's letter is taken off

parts.note: tiddly is British slang for slightly drunk, merry
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: Disapproving sounds as artists lead a tipsy spiritualist away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb but is the metal, and 'medium' looks like a psychic but is a size.
explanation.definitionFit: A rude spluttering sound made with the tongue and lips to show contempt.

clue.text: Find fault in character's weight

indicators.note: in places the fault-finding inside the word for character

parts.note: tone is the character or quality of something
to nag is to keep finding fault

explanation.surface: Criticising the weight of someone's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is a measure of weight, especially of ships or cargo.

clue.text: Savings deposited among the branches?

parts.note: money put by in bank branches, but also a bird's clutch laid up in a tree's branches

explanation.surface: Money paid into several bank branches.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve of money set aside for the future, and literally eggs laid in a home among a tree's boughs.

clue.text: … from festivity, having cheated knight

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
had means tricked or cheated, as in 'you've been had'

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: someone is led away from a celebration having cheated, to the disapproval of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: An earl's out of sauce with distilled anchovies, and his drama's renowned!

indicators.note: out of says the earl's letter leaves the word for sauce

parts.note: sauce is cheek, impudence
E is an abbreviation for earl

indicators.note: distilled takes the essence, the three central letters of the word anchovies

explanation.surface: A garbled recipe note about an earl and an anchovy sauce, ending in praise for a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distilled' as a pick of HOV, the three central letters, is a stretch the blog's commenters also queried.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian author of The Cherry Orchard and Three Sisters is famous for his plays.

clue.text: Brainbox picks out devious thief from vandalised fruit machine

indicators.note: picks out says some letters are taken away from the larger set
devious says the thief's letters are in a twisted order
vandalised says the gaming machine's letters are wrecked and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A clever crook works out how to rob a smashed-up slot machine.
explanation.walkthrough: Take T, H, I, E, F out of FRUIT MACHINE and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainbox is a humorous word for the skull, the box that holds the brain.

clue.text: It's curtains for medication

definitions.meaning: theatre stage curtains are called this

explanation.surface: A grim suggestion that some medicine will be the end of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage curtains in the theatre are called this, and it is also an informal word for tablets.

clue.text: Discussed split with irritant type

indicators.note: discussed means spoken about, so the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave or run away

explanation.surface: Talking about falling out with an annoying sort of person.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect that makes the skin itch is a classic irritant, and the word is used for a pest.

clue.text: Player's line gone astray? Might it be the caddie?

indicators.note: gone astray says the letter for line has wandered off from the player

parts.note: a golfer is a player of golf

explanation.surface: A golfer's shot goes off line; is the caddie to blame?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caddie' suggests golf, the source word, but the answer is a general errand-runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody who runs errands for others, as a caddie fetches and carries for a golfer.

clue.text: Rob worked up part of Heathcliff

indicators.note: worked up in a down clue says the letters run upwards, read in reverse
part of says the letters lie within the name

explanation.surface: A man named Rob getting worked up playing the role of Heathcliff in Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: To filch is to pilfer or steal, which is to rob.

clue.text: Rhubarb plants left among roots of willowherb, azalea and hyacinth

indicators.note: plants means puts something in place among other things
among says the left goes inside the root letters
roots of in a down clue picks the bottom, final, letter of each plant

explanation.surface: A gardening scene: rhubarb set among willowherb, azalea and hyacinth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' looks like a plant among the others; it is the slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for meaningless talk or nonsense, as in actors muttering it on stage.

clue.text: One leaving bar goes after game in the country

indicators.note: goes after says the trimmed bar comes after the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: leaving means the one departs from the bar

parts.note: a rail is a bar
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a pub to follow a sporting match somewhere out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things relating to the countryside rather than towns.

clue.text: The masses vote to follow Independent in Ohio when desperate

indicators.note: in places the independent and the vote inside the jumbled state
when desperate suggests things in a frantic disordered state, so the letters are mixed
to follow puts the vote after the independent

parts.note: a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: The ordinary people go out to vote for an independent candidate in a desperate Ohio election.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is Greek for 'the many' and is used in English for the common people.

clue.text: He bowed, but surely never scraped!

definitions.text: He bowed, but surely never scraped!

parts.words: He bowed, but surely never scraped!
parts.note: bowing and scraping is servility, but here bowed means used a bow on strings and scraped means played badly or scraped by financially

explanation.surface: A proud person who would bow but never grovel.
explanation.definitionFit: A celebrated twentieth-century violinist, who used a bow and was never a mere scraper of the strings.
